title: Research Findings – Taxonomy Discovery Pipeline (US 311617)
purpose: Refine the US 311617 requirements document (inputs, outputs, source handling, reruns, review handoff, validation, ICAO scope, build strategy).

questions.heading: 1. ICAO / CICTT taxonomy status
questions.question: Which version of the CICTT Aviation Occurrence Categories is current, how many categories does it have, what are its coding rules (multi-label, OTHR, UNK, F-POST), and which categories does ICAO treat as highest priority for commercial air transport?

questions.heading: 2. Taxonomies: primary tree vs. facets
questions.question: Which industry taxonomies (CICTT Phase of Flight, ECCAIRS/ADREP, ATA chapters, HFACS, EASA risk areas, NASA ASRS anomaly codes, IATA) should be the primary tree and which should be secondary dimensions or crosswalks?

questions.heading: 3. Public data sources
questions.question: What public aviation safety report sources exist (NTSB, NASA ASRS, FAA AIDS, FAA SDRS, TSB Canada, ATSB, ECCAIRS), and what are their access limits, size, licensing and data-quality issues?

questions.heading: 4. Automated taxonomy discovery (state of the art)
questions.question: What methods build taxonomies or topic hierarchies from text automatically (LLM-based taxonomy generation, clustering, BERTopic, aviation language models), and what are the lessons on reproducibility, stability, human review and evaluation metrics?

questions.heading: 5. Build strategy: most likely path first or the entire tree?
questions.question: Is it better to build a taxonomy top-down, bottom-up, depth-first (most likely path first) or breadth-first (entire tree), and what stopping rules are used?

questions.heading: 6. Governance and AI assurance
questions.question: How are safety taxonomies versioned and change-controlled (CICTT, ECCAIRS), and what AI assurance guidance (EASA AI Concept Paper, FAA) is relevant for an AI-assisted pipeline with human review?
